title: Phase-pure synthesis of arbitrary designed crystalline solids

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a reproducible way to turn a specified inorganic crystal composition and atomic structure into a physical sample of that phase. The input would describe which elements are present and how their atoms are arranged; the output would be a gram-scale sample whose identity and phase purity have been established experimentally. The ambition includes selected metastable crystals: structures that are not the lowest-energy arrangement at their composition but can persist under specified conditions. This is a proposed capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

Conceptual synthesis: making the correct elemental composition is insufficient. The same elements can form different crystal structures, and a sample can contain several phases whose combined composition resembles the target. A successful structure-to-solid method must therefore control which phase forms and distinguish the intended crystal from alternative structures and mixtures of known phases. Here, phase purity concerns the crystalline phases present; it does not automatically imply a defect-free single crystal or complete control over every atom.

The historical motivation is the gap between computational materials discovery and experimental access. Merchant and colleagues’ 2023 GNoME paper expanded the set of predicted inorganic structures while identifying synthesizability, phase transitions and dynamic stability as continuing challenges. Computational stability prediction supplies candidate targets; it does not itself provide a reliable synthesis route. The word “arbitrary” expresses the broad ambition, while any actual method would have a demonstrated domain of compositions, structures and processing conditions.

significance.text: Merchant and colleagues described inorganic crystal discovery in 2023 as constrained by expensive trial-and-error approaches and by the cost, throughput and complications of experimental synthesis and cataloguing. Against that historical background, a reliable structure-to-solid method would change access to designed materials: within its demonstrated domain, a structural specification could become a repeatable manufacturing target instead of the starting point for an uncertain, bespoke synthesis campaign.

Conditional impact synthesis: the direct consequence would be access to the intended solid in enough quantity for repeatable characterization and subsequent experiments. That would make it easier to test whether predicted structures exist, compare competing property predictions and investigate relationships between composition, structure and behavior. Reproducible access could also reduce the time spent repeatedly rediscovering workable preparation conditions. These benefits depend on actual synthesis breadth, reliability and cost.

The ability to include metastable targets would extend access beyond ground-state structures. The readable supplementary material described in the supplied review notes that metastable inorganic crystals can be viable for industrial applications. This supports retaining metastability as part of the ambition, but it does not establish a general method for producing such phases or guarantee that any particular metastable target will be useful.

Conditional impact synthesis: programmable access to a crystal would not guarantee superconductivity, useful ionic conductivity, catalytic activity or device performance. Those properties require separate measurements, and practical utility can additionally depend on defects, interfaces, morphology, environmental stability and processing. The analogy to programmable manufacture is therefore bounded: the proposed advance concerns reliable production of a specified crystalline phase, with gram-scale success still leaving larger-scale economics and device integration to be demonstrated.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability, as formulated here, is a general and reproducible route from a crystal specification to a verified phase-pure sample, including selected metastable targets. GNoME’s 2023 conclusion identifies synthesizability alongside phase transitions and stability contributions from vibrations and configurational entropy as unresolved challenges. That historical account motivates the goal, but the supplied evidence does not establish whether the complete capability remains absent as of November 1, 2026.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: a calculated stability ranking does not specify the reaction pathway that will produce a crystal. A synthesis method must select precursors and processing conditions that allow the intended phase to nucleate and grow while limiting competing products. Temperature, pressure, chemical environment, transport and reaction time can affect which structure forms. For a metastable target, the method must also find a preparation and recovery window in which the desired phase forms and survives rather than converting to a competing phase.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: the target specification itself needs physical boundaries. A relaxed calculated structure may change at the temperature or pressure of synthesis or measurement, and its stability may depend on effects omitted from a particular calculation. A convincing method must distinguish failure to find a route from a target that cannot persist under the declared output conditions. No synthesis process should be expected to produce every mathematically specified arrangement of atoms as a recoverable bulk solid.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: identification and reproducibility are separate barriers from initially obtaining a promising sample. Diffraction must distinguish the proposed structure from plausible alternative phases and mixtures; composition measurements and complementary characterization may be needed where diffraction is ambiguous. Moving to gram quantities must preserve phase composition across the batch and across repeated preparations. A single suggestive pattern or a small amount of target material embedded in other products would not satisfy the proposed capability.

current_state.text: In the peer-reviewed 2023 paper “Scaling deep learning for materials discovery,” Merchant and colleagues reported 381,000 new entries on an updated computational convex hull. This is a computational stability result, not a count of synthesized or phase-pure materials. The paper also reported a final energy-prediction mean absolute error of 11 meV per atom on relaxed structures. The 11 meV figure measures prediction error; it is not a characteristic energy of the proposed materials and does not quantify synthesis reliability.

The authors reported 736 matches between GNoME structures and independently obtained experimental structures in the Inorganic Crystal Structure Database, using a database query from January 2023. Of these matches, 184 corresponded to experimental discoveries since the project began. These comparisons connect predictions with experimental realizations, but they are not evidence of 736 prospective synthesis successes directed by GNoME. They also do not establish a general preparation route, gram-scale output or verified phase purity for those materials.

The same paper identified experimental cataloguing constraints involving cost, throughput and synthesis complications, and retained synthesizability as an open challenge in 2023. It therefore supports a historical prediction-to-synthesis gap. It does not directly quantify how much faster prediction is than synthesis and identification, nor establish that discovery in 2026 is predominantly calculation followed by bespoke synthesis. No supplied update establishes the field’s position on the full proposed capability as of November 1, 2026.

The supplied review reports complete retained main-article text and Methods in both HTML and PDF, despite cookie-related redirects in the recorded retrieval URLs. Its supplementary evidence is narrower: the retained supplementary representation was partial, with an extraction warning concerning skipped form content, and figures were uninspected. The readable supplementary passage supports the relevance of metastable crystals, but no additional conclusions about supplementary figures or unextracted content are warranted.

The supplied material does not verify the earlier attribution to Antypov, Rosseinsky and colleagues, or establish the contents or retrieval history of the mentioned 2024 autonomous-laboratory critique. Neither is used here to judge demonstrated synthesis performance. These evidence gaps do not show that the attributed statements or critique are false, and they do not invalidate the dated GNoME results.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed milestone: provide 50 computationally specified crystal structures spanning several structure types, and obtain at least half as phase-pure gram-scale samples. The set should include some targets absent from experimental databases and some explicitly selected metastable targets. The target count, one-half success threshold and gram scale are proposed criteria, not established standards. Passing would demonstrate substantial breadth toward the concept; a finite selected set cannot establish literal synthesis of arbitrary crystalline solids.
completion_criteria.label: At least half of 50 targets yield phase-pure gram-scale samples

completion_criteria.text: Proposed benchmark design: fix the target-selection procedure before synthesis and report every attempted target, including failures. Define the range of chemistries and structure types, how prior experimental knowledge is handled, and which database versions are used to assess whether a target was previously recorded. Define metastability relative to a stated computational or experimental reference and specify the conditions under which the product must persist. These choices should make the benchmark’s coverage and difficulty assessable rather than allowing success to depend on selecting only convenient targets.
completion_criteria.label: Target selection is fixed and every synthesis attempt reported

completion_criteria.text: Proposed identity and purity demonstration: specify an operational phase-purity threshold, measurement sensitivity and uncertainty before evaluating the samples. Supply diffraction data and structural analyses that test the intended phase against plausible alternatives, including mixtures of known phases. Use composition measurements and complementary structural methods where necessary to resolve ambiguity, and account for potential amorphous or otherwise undetected material. Report the recovered amount that actually meets the declared criteria, rather than treating the total reaction-product mass as target yield.
completion_criteria.label: Target identity and recovered yield meet prespecified phase-purity criteria

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility demonstration: repeat preparations in independent batches, publish sufficient synthesis and characterization detail for replication, and obtain independent laboratory reproduction across a meaningful subset of targets. Report success rates, variability and the extent of manual intervention. A claim of a general method should distinguish transferable route selection from a collection of separately optimized recipes.
completion_criteria.label: Independent laboratories reproduce synthesis across a meaningful target subset

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: declare permitted temperatures, pressures, atmospheres, precursors, processing times and recovery conditions, together with product stability during storage and measurement. For metastable phases, show survival through isolation and the stated characterization interval. Gram-scale production should be demonstrated directly; larger-scale manufacture, economic competitiveness, useful functional properties and device performance would require additional evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Practical limits are declared and metastable survival through characterization demonstrated

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-01, “A method that predicts realistic chemical outcomes before the experiment,” overlaps with predicting synthesis outcomes and selecting routes. CHEMREV-09 requires the additional physical result: the specified crystalline phase must actually be produced and identified. Computational structure stability and realistic reaction-outcome prediction can inform that task, but neither alone establishes experimental access.

Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-04, “Practical, on-demand synthesis of arbitrary stable molecules,” shares the ambition of making a chemical specification reliably accessible. Its stated target is discrete molecules; CHEMREV-09 concerns extended crystalline solids, where composition alone does not determine crystal structure or exclude phase mixtures. CHEMREV-11, “General, predictive functionalization of a chosen unactivated C–H bond in a complex molecule,” concerns selective molecular transformation and remains a distinct capability.

Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-10, “Positional chemical manufacture of macroscopic, atomically specified matter,” has a more extensive manufacturing target than producing a phase-pure crystal. CHEMREV-09 could be achieved through controlled bulk chemical processing without atom-by-atom placement or arbitrary spatial patterning. It does not by itself promise atomically specified devices, interfaces or macroscopic objects. This comparison is based on the supplied title; a full CHEMREV-10 definition was not provided.

Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-03, “A manufacturable room-temperature superconductor at ambient pressure,” and CHEMREV-08, “A rechargeable air-breathing battery with aviation-relevant specific energy,” could benefit from access to candidate crystalline materials. Their completion depends on functional performance and manufacturing or system requirements beyond phase synthesis. Making a candidate crystal does not establish superconductivity, battery specific energy or practical operation.

Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-05, “Enzyme-level catalysts on request for arbitrary reactions,” concerns catalytic performance, while CHEMREV-06 on competitive mild nitrogen fixation, CHEMREV-07 on multicarbon chemicals from CO2 and water, and CHEMREV-12 on methane-to-methanol conversion concern particular productive chemical processes. CHEMREV-13 concerns returning commodity plastics to monomers below virgin-production cost and energy. Designed crystalline solids might contribute catalysts or other materials to some of these goals, but producing those solids would not demonstrate the required reaction selectivity, throughput, energy use or economics.

Roster-based synthesis: CHEMREV-02, “Open-ended Darwinian evolution in a synthetic chemical system,” concerns sustained evolutionary behavior. A crystal-synthesis method might use iterative search or optimization, but that would not establish Darwinian evolution in the chemical system itself. The supplied roster gives no basis for merging this concept with CHEMREV-09.

change_log.change: Preserved CHEMREV-09, its title and its central ambition of reproducible synthesis and identification of designed crystalline phases.
change_log.reason: The concept remains coherent and motivated by the documented historical synthesis challenge, even where individual supporting assertions require correction.

change_log.change: Corrected 11 meV per atom from an energy value to the reported final energy-prediction mean absolute error on relaxed structures.
change_log.reason: The supplied review identifies the quantity explicitly as a model-error metric.

change_log.change: Separated the 381,000 computational convex-hull entries from experimental production, and explained the retrospective context of the 736 experimental matches, including the 184 discoveries since project initiation.
change_log.reason: These figures do not establish prospective GNoME-directed synthesis, gram-scale output or phase purity.

change_log.change: Replaced unqualified present-day claims about discovery practice and relative prediction speed with the documented 2023 bottleneck and an explicit limit on knowledge of the field in November 2026.
change_log.reason: The supplied historical source does not quantify comparative speeds or establish the capability’s present-day absence.

change_log.change: Integrated metastability, phase identity, competing mixtures and the distinction between phase purity and atomically specified manufacture into the explanation and barriers.
change_log.reason: These distinctions clarify what the proposed synthesis capability must accomplish and prevent it from being confused with composition control or positional manufacturing.

change_log.change: Retained the 50-target, one-half-success, gram-scale milestone while adding explicit metastable coverage, operational characterization, reproducibility and practical-boundary proposals.
change_log.reason: The original benchmark is useful as a proposed milestone but needs defined evaluation conditions and cannot establish universality.

change_log.change: Separated direct access to a solid from conditional scientific, functional and manufacturing benefits.
change_log.reason: Successful synthesis does not guarantee superconductivity, ionic conductivity, catalysis, device performance or economic scale-up.

change_log.change: Removed the unverified Antypov/Rosseinsky attribution and the asserted critique-retrieval history from the scientific evidence narrative while preserving their uncertainty.
change_log.reason: No supplied source substantiates those statements; this omission does not imply they are false.

change_log.change: Preserved the supplementary extraction and inspection limitations reported by the review.
change_log.reason: The readable metastability passage can be used, but unextracted content and uninspected figures cannot support further conclusions.

change_log.change: Added roster-based overlap and boundary explanations without merging any concepts.
change_log.reason: The related entries distinguish predictive methods, molecular synthesis, functional materials, chemical processes and positional manufacture from this phase-synthesis goal.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish whether the full proposed structure-to-phase capability remains unmet as of November 1, 2026; no freshness search record was supplied.
The comparative speed of computational prediction versus experimental synthesis and identification is not quantified by the supplied evidence.
The benchmark still requires final choices for target selection, chemistry coverage, permitted prior knowledge, phase-purity thresholds, detection limits and independent replication breadth.

The physical admissibility of targets and the allowed range and persistence of metastability need explicit definitions; “arbitrary” cannot reasonably include structures that cannot persist under the declared conditions.
The Antypov/Rosseinsky attribution and the contents and retrieval history of the mentioned 2024 autonomous-laboratory critique remain unverified.

The supplementary representation described by the review is partial and its figures were uninspected, despite the source index listing no extraction issues. The more specific review limitation is retained.
Only roster titles were supplied for related concepts, so their detailed scope, particularly CHEMREV-10, cannot be fully compared.

brief.title: Making crystals to match an atomic blueprint
possible: Researchers could specify a solid’s ingredients and atomic arrangement, then reliably obtain a gram-scale sample of the intended crystal. They could test a designed material without first having to discover a workable preparation recipe.

This would include selected metastable crystals: arrangements that can persist even though another arrangement has lower energy. Samples would be checked for phase purity, meaning they contain the intended crystal structure rather than a mixture of structures.
why: Reliable access would let researchers test whether predicted crystals exist and whether their measured properties match predictions. Repeatable preparation would make comparisons easier and reduce time spent rediscovering workable recipes.

sources.showed: Their machine-learning system identified 381,000 additional crystal structures calculated to be stable against competing structures and mixtures.
sources.quote: Of the stable structures, 736 have already been independently experimentally realized.
sources.cited_for: Computer predictions provide a large pool of candidate crystals, with some matching independently made materials.
sources.not_established: Matching predictions to existing experimental structures does not establish a reliable route to making pure samples.

sources.showed: Their autonomous powder laboratory reported making 36 target compounds. Many successful samples also contained substantial unwanted products.
sources.quote: many of the samples contain prominent byproducts
sources.cited_for: Robotics and automated recipe selection can turn selected computational targets into physical materials.
sources.not_established: Producing a target within a mixture does not establish phase purity or reliable synthesis across arbitrary designs.

sources.showed: In a preprint, they reported that choosing starting materials to avoid competing products often improved crystal purity in robotic synthesis.
sources.quote: Our predicted precursors frequently yield target materials with higher phase purity
sources.cited_for: Choosing starting materials using calculated reaction pathways can improve synthesis outcomes.
sources.not_established: The tests cover selected material families, and the metastable targets gave low yields.

sources.showed: In a preprint, they made metastable layered crystals by exchanging atoms in an existing crystal. The magnesium–zirconium product also contained another structure.
sources.quote:
The LiBr can be washed away with water
without changing the MgZrN 2 structures (Figure S1).
sources.cited_for: An existing crystal can serve as a template for making a metastable structure that survives recovery.
sources.not_established: This targeted route does not establish pure products or a general method for metastable crystals.

sources.showed: In a preprint, they reported autonomous growth of thin films containing only the intended metastable crystal phase, using live images to adjust growth conditions.
sources.quote:
Our scheme regularly resulted in > 30-fold reduction in the number of experiments 
compared to comprehensive parameter-space mapping.
sources.cited_for: Feedback during growth can guide an automated laboratory toward a selected metastable crystal phase.
sources.not_established: Success with a selected thin film does not establish gram-scale bulk synthesis or broad coverage of crystal designs.

shown: Szymanski and colleagues’ A-Lab demonstrates automated preparation across a varied target set, but many products were mixtures. Liang and colleagues report pure metastable thin films in a preprint. These results demonstrate parts of the capability in different settings.
missing: A broadly applicable method must turn atomic blueprints into pure gram-scale samples, including selected metastable crystals.
Measurements must distinguish the intended structure from alternatives and establish how much recovered material meets the purity requirement.
Independent laboratories must reproduce the results across a meaningful range of targets.

milestones.label: Pure gram-scale samples from at least half the targets
milestones.explanation: At least half the benchmark targets would have to yield pure gram-scale samples across varied structures, including previously unrecorded and metastable targets. This would demonstrate breadth beyond isolated successes.

milestones.label: Fixed target selection and complete reporting
milestones.explanation: Target selection, allowed prior knowledge and product survival conditions would have to be fixed beforehand, with every attempt reported. This would make coverage and difficulty assessable.

milestones.label: Measured identity, purity and recovered yield
milestones.explanation: Samples would have to meet predefined identity and purity criteria that account for alternative structures and undetected material. This would establish how much qualifying target material was actually recovered.

milestones.label: Independent laboratories reproduce a meaningful subset
milestones.explanation: Independent batches and laboratories would have to reproduce a meaningful target subset, with variability and human intervention reported. This would test whether the method transfers beyond its developers.

milestones.label: Declared operating limits and demonstrated metastable survival
milestones.explanation: Gram-scale products would have to survive recovery, storage and measurement under declared operating limits. This would establish the conditions under which the method delivers usable samples.

uncertain: Which designed structures can physically persist under the required output conditions?
What purity threshold, measurement sensitivity and breadth of independent replication would establish success?
How broadly can route selection transfer between material families without separately optimizing every recipe?
